text:
Jamie Oleksiak, the Big Rig, came to Vancouver after five seasons in Seattle, and he's been exactly what he was there: a big, physical defenseman who hits and blocks and doesn't produce much. He has eight points in 23 games, 40 hits and 31 blocks.

The on-ice picture is better than it looks. Vancouver gets 45% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, a poor number on its own, but almost eight points better than when he sits. The Canucks have also scored 6.1 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on, so his points are probably light.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has the two sides of him: he stopped 18% of the zone entries aimed at him last season (typical is 11%), and kept possession on only 26% of his exits.

His minutes dropped to about 15 over the last ten, then jumped to 20:18 against Minnesota on Nov 21. What to watch: whether that was a one-night need or a sign the Canucks trust him more.
